svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Why a 75% cut in cache-read prices cuts an agentic-coding bill by about 72%
svg.desc: Illustrative arithmetic based on Max Woolf's estimate that cache reads are 96 to 99 percent of agentic-coding token spend. Before: a bill of 100 units, 96 of them cache reads and 4 everything else (input, output, cache writes). After a 75 percent cut to cache-read prices only: cache reads cost 24 units and everything else still 4, for a total of 28 units, 72 percent lower. At a 99 percent cache share the drop is about 74 percent.
svg.text: Cache reads are most of an agent's bill, so cutting them cuts the bill
Illustrative arithmetic on Max Woolf's estimate (Oct 25, 2026): cache reads = 96–99% of agentic-coding token spend
Total = 28 units → 72% lower (≈74% if cache share is 99%)
Assumes only the cache-read price changes. Woolf cites Anthropic's Sept 1 cut of cache reads from $1 to $0.25 per million tokens (75%)
and estimates a ~70–75% drop in real agent costs. His 96–99% figure is an estimate; coverage disagrees on whether it is tokens or dollars.
